subject: NimbleBio POC: MAP orientation & success roster
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nimblebio.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Lena Park <lena@nimblebio.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro & MAP orientation for NimbleBio POC

Hi Kimberly —

Really excited to get the POC moving. Quick context: NimbleBio is evaluating a document-extraction assistant (clinical notes -> structured events) and we want to validate accuracy, latency, and cost before committing to a production rollout. We put together a rough scope and would like to align on a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that covers owners, success criteria, bench plan (prompts / evals), and the close timeline.

High-level success criteria we care about:
- Extraction accuracy (entity-level recall/precision) across a 5k-record benchmark — target: >= 0.88 F1 for core entities
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 512-token context
- Cost: inference cost per 1k tokens under $5 (target to be refined)
- Stability: no more than 2% failure rate over 48-hour soak test

Can we do a short MAP kickoff tomorrow or Wednesday? We’d like owners assigned for:
- Evaluation bench and prompts (who curates prompts / golden labels)
- Runtime acceptance / latency SLOs
- Integration + security signoff (data flows)

I attached a one-page scope and a starter MAP from our side.

Two quick asks for the kickoff:
1) Please confirm Redwood owners and suggested meeting time.
2) Any immediate blockers from compliance we should know about (SOC2, data retention, encryption at rest)?

Thanks —
Sanjay Rao
Director of Product
NimbleBio

Attachments: nimblebio-poc-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro & MAP orientation for NimbleBio POC

Hi Sanjay — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear scope. We can absolutely run a focused MAP kickoff to lock owners and measurable goals. Proposed Redwood roster for the MAP:

- Executive sponsor / commercial lead: Kimberly Park (kimberly_park@redwood.com) — overall timeline, contract checkpoints
- Evaluation bench / prompts lead: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) — will own the eval harness, prompt set, and golden labels alignment
- Runtime SLOs / infra lead: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com) — latency targets, soak test coordination, and resource sizing for Dedicated or Private options
- Integration & data-security liaison: Priyom Das (priyom_das@redwood.com) — data flows, minimal sample requirements, and SOC2 evidence requests

Attached: nimblebio-map-template-v1.docx (MAP template) and a draft schedule in the sheet you shared. I copied high-level, editable success criteria below and added a couple Redwood-specific acceptance checks.

Draft success criteria (editable):
- Entity-level F1 >= 0.88 across agreed 5k benchmark (Marissa to confirm sampling plan)
- p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 512 tokens across a mixed-workload 30-minute window (Vivek to provide test harness)
- Inference cost estimate <= $5 per 1k tokens on the reference throughput profile (billing estimate and quantization options to be provided by Redwood)
- Soak test: 48-hour run with failure rate <2% and KV-cache hit-rate baseline > 70% (operational metric)
- Security: Redwood to provide SOC2 artifact list; NimbleBio to confirm minimal sample obfuscation plan (Priyom will coordinate)

Proposed next steps:
1) 60-minute kickoff — agenda: introductions, review success criteria, owners sign-off, confirm benchmark set, and schedule two-week sprint for prompt curation. Suggested slot: Wed 12/1 10:00–11:00 PT.
2) Marissa to share initial prompt set and golden-label schema within 48 hours after kickoff.
3) Vivek to publish a latency/soak test plan and expected infra config within 72 hours.

I’ll upload the MAP template to the shared Drive and create a HubSpot MAP record (link below). Do you want Redwood to lead the first two-week sprint for prompt collection or would NimbleBio prefer to? Either option works; we often pair engineers and product folks to speed labeling.

Link to MAP doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Nx-ExampleSharedDoc
HubSpot MAP record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8791/NB-2026-0421

If that time works, I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the MAP.

Thanks — I look forward to working together.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Intro & MAP orientation for NimbleBio POC — owners + immediate asks

Team — forwarding NimbleBio's kickoff note and the draft MAP I just sent. Please see proposed owner list above. Action items (please reply with ETA by EOD today):

- Marissa: confirm sampling approach for the 5k benchmark (dev/test split, anonymization constraints) and share example prompt set by EOD 12/2. Include who from NimbleBio will provide golden labels vs. what Redwood can label.
- Vivek: outline a 30-minute mixed-load harness and a 48-hour soak test plan, with infra sizing (Dedicated vs hosted burst) and expected p95 baselines. Need this by COB 12/3 so we can schedule the soak slot the following week.
- Priyom: list the SOC2 artifacts NimbleBio will need and the minimal sample obfuscation approach. Also confirm whether NimbleBio requires on-prem/private deployment for samples. Response by EOD 12/3.

Notes: keep the prompts representative of clinical note variability (abbreviations, misspellings). Marissa — reach out to Lena and Sanjay to confirm whether they have a labeled subset already.

Thanks — I’ll consolidate responses and then send the calendar invite for Wed 12/1 10:00 PT (tentative until we hear back).

Hi Kimberly / team —

Thanks for the quick reply and proposed owners — that looks good to us. Wed 12/1 10:00 PT works for the core kickoff — I accepted the calendar invite. A few clarifications from NimbleBio:

- We have a small, partially-labeled subset (~800 records) we can share as a seed. Marissa, we can coordinate how to transfer sample labels (SFTP or secure Share).
- On compliance: NimbleBio is SOC2 Type II in progress; we will need a short artifact list from Priyom for our security review. We are open to Redwood providing redacted samples if needed.
- For success criteria: the 0.88 F1 is our target but we are open to an initial calibration run (first 500 samples) to set final thresholds.

Looking forward to the kickoff. After that meeting we’d like to lock the two-week prompt sprint and target a technical review with our infra team on 12/9.

Best,
Lena Park
Product Manager — NimbleBio
